en: Three ears held no thought,
Our people were broken in our time,
Thinking, his heart became a burning coal,
The mother's whole body burned into blood,
The age was left without remedy,
Its foundation strayed through falsehood.
Do not speak an evil word,
The khan’s sons
Saying they would bring him out,
What inheritance will he attain?
To his mottled horse, great as a mountain,
The fanged enemy left the mark of his strength,
Uncle, where will he abandon him?
The offspring of the noble prince,
Is there still a day for us to see?
Where is the place to which we shall go?
The khan’s sons,
Is there no one who will take heart?
Leave your breast to the darkness,
Is there any hope for us to enter?
Then Jeljetpes spoke at that moment:
Noble gray-maned twins,
O vast ones who could shatter the world,
If you fight, listen, lion-hearted men,
Who would listen to these words of yours?
Ah, let the accursed night hear it,
Let the hard black earth hear it,
My twin heroes, what do you say?
A curse upon the mighty Chinese,
His fist against their dark eyes,
I hurled the stone straight at him.
Will the raider truly come?
Will a man grapple with him?
Can he take command of countless souls?
Will the khan strike at the tidings?
How could a soul not die there?
Even grappling with him, they cannot prevail,
From the lament of this great multitude,
The people dug the length of a hero,
Even seizing him, they cannot prevail,
From the anguish of this multitude,
Will he not sweep every side?
Will he not carry out his settled intent?
The Kyrgyz children upon the mountain pasture,
Without leaving even what remained behind,
If they strike at evening, no horse remains,
No sound tear remains in the eye,
The remedy to be found now,
The hour when you will truly see,
Would he not scatter it in place of water?
My fate touched by the komuz,
Would the remaining Kyrgyz not see it?
Your cherished life that was taken,
God the sovereign, the Creator,
Whatever He has written,
Death together with torment,
At last the poor man arrived,
Showing his face to the sun,
The true racehorse carried his hand onward,
Chyntemir in his bearing,
Made his wrath known to the people,
With no inhabitant and no assembly,
He appeared and set it burning,
He pressed behind the battle cry,
Let Arby slaughter his elder brother,
That he left his town behind him,
You poured out your fierce wrath,
The few Kyrgyz of Ala-Too,
They made a people rooted at the foundation,
They brought the unsteady hero low,
Like a soul hardened by enemies,
When a lone soul remained standing,
He carved it himself into the fire,
The horde destroyed this,
Manas took it after reflection,
His devastated people took it,
As we stood witnessing, it faded,
If so, we cannot remain standing,
Of this remnant left by Chyntemir,
The two heroes took what they wished,
Zhelzhetpes pursued his enemy,
He would not let the camel's mouth be muzzled.
When his fierce anger blazed,
He would not break before the onslaught,
He would not make enemies of those on earth,
Separated from the people of his land,
Let us reach the hard road of sorrow,
Come, hero, let us go!
For the soul so grievously watched,
Let us leave the birch grove behind,
Let us become wretches bereft of the hero,
Let us disperse before being destroyed,
Let me prepare the gaze of the restless one.
His soul crawled from afar,
Seeking a people among whom to settle,
Sustaining the life of their chief hero,
Heroic sons, let us go.
From the world near Ala-Too,
We departed as his word directed,
Driving livestock away from its abundance.
When they emerged from being watched,
Your eyes drew many souls onward,
Let us reach the hard birch country,
From the harsh halt of the wrathful one,
Saying this, let us depart.
Thus spoke Jeljetpes,
Addressing all three with his words,
Displaying his eloquence,
Persuading the twins to heed him,
Toward the place where the sun rises over the world,
Turning their faces toward the west,
Seeking a pass that would shelter them,
Seeking the pass where the sun sets,
Seeking a land in which to sustain life,
Taking the red camel and the swift hound,
Loading precious gold and jewels,
We shall not fall away from nobility,
We shall move the village and roam,
At dawn he led the way,
My God, the Kyrgyz were a treasure.
Unable to take the people, he grieved.
Separated from the people of the royal camp,
He wrapped his turban and departed.
They lamented rightly, vast as Samarkand.
Faithless Bakadar,
Separated from the people of the royal camp.
The young man Dostan took the road.
He never turned and drew another man along.
The two companions entered misery.
While crossing hill after hill,
They camped across the moonlit steppe.
He was departing from abundance.
They clustered like silver maral.
The finest one among the Kyrgyz people,
He was departing into nothingness.
The looming mountain was high.
Seeing the land, he wept once.
Tears streamed from both eyes,
Bloody tears mingled with blood.
Like horses ready at the tether,
God breathed; all the people gathered.
The netted eye could not open.
The sound of lament would not cease.
The Kyrgyz people had many daughters.
For a brave man, the hardship was immense.
His head passed among the stones.
The honor of the Kyrgyz purpose,
A sack of hardship fell upon his head.
Let us feast together, poor people.
He left it behind for the people.
The place to which the company migrated was far.
He left his homeland behind.
A thousand treasures, ten thousand possessions,
He abandoned them and departed.
For the white dream and the fading soul,
Two champions born as twins,
Immeasurable, beyond the wind’s reach,
The twins lamented in grief,
Separated from their people and homeland.
The abandoned one is going away,
A thousand marks of tears from the eyes,
He goes onward upon his road,
The many people in the sun's contentment,
His neighing horse is departing,
This is an age of words for the bereft,
People do not scatter words and sayings,
The broad-circling stormy eye,
You will come shining, dear Kenen,
His body has gone toward the enemy,
Descending from the darkened soul,
His body belongs among the Chinese people,
Turning back proved a heavy hardship,
His body belonged to a warrior people,
The hero rolled up the saddlebags,
We are setting out and leaving,
Stand offering reverence with awe,
We are leaving them behind,
Driving them backward from grave to grave,
Giving the Kyrgyz over to the enemy,
Leaving them when hardship arrived,
Leading them into the desert,
Zhelzhetpes in the place of a father,
Bracing them with his support,
Leaving no hill or ridge behind,
Bearing the inherited land upon his back,
Suffering torment and turning pale,
Bringing back my blue-gray eyes,
His sword became the work of the Kyrgyz,
Poor Kenen's soul went to China,
No life remained in the struggle,
He is going away as a captive,
The dark Chinese knew no restraint,
He goes on in wrath,
His heart fell into sorrow,
Closing his eyes upon countless wealth,
His eyes were sated with whiteness,
A dark clamor stretched into writing,
It came from the beloved people.
With eyes fixed ahead as the days flew by,
Streaming onward as though life would turn back,
Appearing close before their brows,
Crossing hill after hill and mountain,
Fording fiercely flowing water,
The noble twins,
The gray-maned heroes upon the earth
Were all traveling onward,
Finding rest in a comfortable land,
They traveled on in ease.
Renowned as extraordinary souls,
Without looking back at the world they left,
They traveled on through the passing hour,
Guarding themselves like wary souls,
They went onward like the wind,
What would happen if they went to Talas?
Seeking their own Kyrgyz people,
Traveling on foot south of Talas,
This was their torment, this was their great trial,
If such a fate came upon anyone,
For the sake of days beyond Aktarat,
Finding it grievously difficult,
Coming from the people of the horde,
Without speaking broadly or uttering a word,
They went onward like the dead,
Into a plain beyond the reach of sight,
Paying no heed to anything the ear heard,
When they loaded their burdens, the pasture was high,
The migrating train went over the heights,
Left on the steppe beneath the sun,
Their people, their land, and their lineage
Fled onward like deer,
With nothing else in their thoughts,
Departing amid unending sorrow,
Traveling for months through stony country,
They went onward like the dead.
Now the fourth assembly gathered,
My child came into their hands,
Clicking his palate as water gathers,
He opened wide his eyes and mouth,
When it appeared, the deed became hardship,
The deed came into order,
Living, he truly stood in hell,
Hope itself became hardship,
He cries out amid the plunder,
Setting his bent back against it,
His people burned and rolled away,
He left wealth vast as a horde,
His voice changed within the forest,
Red snow gathered as it was sharpened,
The komuz broke in the desert,
This hardship was hell to behold,
That bay horse bore what strength remained,
It bit and went away, lamenting,
The hound stood sated in the middle,
He was a champion burning in grief,
Alas, my strength on the day of hardship,
An iron-like mound gathered,
